questions.q: Per this lesson, what's the main problem with reviewing a migration script right before deployment?
options: Only junior developers write migration scripts, so review is unnecessary
By that point, schema decisions are already baked into weeks of application code, so fixing a real problem means reopening finished work
Migration scripts can't be reviewed at all once written
It's actually the ideal time, earlier review causes more problems
questions.explain: Late review can still catch show-stoppers, but it rarely improves the design because so much is already committed by that point.

questions.q: What does it mean for a DBA to be involved earlier, per this lesson?
options: Being consulted during sprint planning or design discussions, before code gets written
Replacing the development team's project manager
Attending every single team meeting indefinitely with no exceptions
Writing all application code themselves instead of developers
questions.explain: Even a standing short slot or a channel to ping before writing a migration moves the conversation earlier, before code is written.

questions.q: What is an 'N+1 pattern', as described in this lesson?
options: A database table with N+1 columns
A type of index used for full-text search
An application firing many small queries where one well-designed query would do
A naming convention for foreign keys
questions.explain: The lesson's example fires one query for the order and then N more queries, one per order line, instead of a single combined query.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that understanding query patterns matters as much as understanding the schema?
options: SQL Server ignores schema design and only cares about queries
A normalized schema can still perform badly in production if the application's actual access pattern fights it
Query patterns are more important than schema and should replace it entirely
Developers are not allowed to write their own queries
questions.explain: A DBA who only looks at CREATE TABLE statements sees half the picture; how the app queries that schema is the other half.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does effective day-to-day collaboration with a dev team actually require from a DBA?
options: A formal weekly audit of every table in the database
Showing up to the right conversations and asking how something will be queried before it's designed
No collaboration at all — DBAs should work entirely independently
Full authority to reject any developer's pull request without explanation
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a smaller time investment than fixing a bad design in production later, achieved through timely, informed conversations.
